messages:
jose (ACME): hey team — after the model rollout last night our codegen integration started producing code that fails to compile. this is blocking our CI for several repos. any idea?

alice (CS): sorry to hear that — can you paste the prompt + the exact model id you saw in the API response? and one failing generated snippet + the compiler error?

jose (ACME): sure. model in response header: gpt-code-3-redwood-v2.3. prompt (shortened): 

```
// generate a TypeScript function to call our payments API and return parsed json
function createPayment(amount, currency, customerId) {
  // ...
}
```

response (generated):

```ts
import fetch from 'node-fetch';

async function createPayment(amount: number, currency: string) {
  const res = await fetch(`/internal/payments/create`, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ amount, currency }),
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
  });
  const body = await res.json();
  return body.data; // <-- missing typings and customerId usage
}
```

compiler output from our CI (tsc):

```
src/payments.ts(12,7): error TS2339: Property 'data' does not exist on type 'unknown'.
src/payments.ts(4,34): error TS2554: Expected 3 arguments, but got 2.
```

jose (ACME): two problems: missing use of customerId param and assumption that body has .data. previous model (v2.1) generated correct signature and parsing. style drift too — variable names and comment patterns changed.

brian (ML eng): thanks, jose. cc: @tanya. preliminary guess: v2.3 had a small decoding tweak and a different default sampling config for code models. some heuristics that previously injected type-safe parsing were relaxed in the new variant. can you also send the raw API request+response headers (we need request_id)?

jose (ACME): request_id: req_8a7f23b2, timestamp 2026-01-29T03:42:10Z. full request (sanitized) is attached in their support ticket IN-ACME-4721.

deploy-bot: deploy event: gpt-code-3-redwood-v2.3 promoted to production (rollout id: roll_2026_01_28_23).

alice (CS): @brian @tanya we have ACME in a pretty bad spot — multiple repos failing CI. they want either a rollback for their org or an immediate mitigation. can we pin them to the prior model (v2.1) while we investigate? what's the fastest path?

tanya (SRE): checking telemetry — I see a +27% spike in stderr/compile_fails for codegen routes from 2026-01-28 23:05 UTC coincident with roll_2026_01_28_23. affected orgs: ACME (heavy), two other customers (low). latency is normal, it's purely generation content differences. we can create a routing override to pin ACME to v2.1 (config change). impact low.

brian (ML eng): action plan: 1) reproduce locally with the exact prompt + model v2.3 and compare to v2.1; 2) run a diff tool on ASTs to isolate why customerId dropped and why body typed unknown; 3) if it's a model behavior change we roll a targeted rollback/pin for affected orgs and file a model-debugging ticket with the inference team. I'll start reproducing now.

jose (ACME): appreciate it. timeline? our release window is tomorrow morning. if pin is possible please do it ASAP.

alice (CS): @tanya please do the pin and notify ACME when done. I'll keep them updated. also adding workaround: ask ACME to add a small guard in the prompt like: 

"Always include all input parameters in function signature and use safe parsing: const body = await res.json() as { data?: any }"

that should buy time but not ideal.

tanya (SRE): pinned ACME to gpt-code-3-redwood-v2.1 via routing override roll_ovr_1759009900 (applied at 2026-01-29T03:45:00Z). rolling back only for their org. notified infra team for audit.

deploy-bot: routing override applied: roll_ovr_1759009900 -> org: acme-corp, model: gpt-code-3-redwood-v2.1, effective: 2026-01-29T03:45:00Z.

brian (ML eng): reproduced locally. differences: v2.3 has a reduced "extraction bias" for parameter usage, which made it prune what it considered unused args; also default schema/typing hints were slightly downgraded. attaching diff snippet: 

```diff
- function createPayment(amount: number, currency: string, customerId: string) {
+ function createPayment(amount: number, currency: string) {
   // ...
 }
```

brian (ML eng): root cause likely a small change in the code model's instruction-following head where a recent fine-tune deprioritized long signatures. filing internal ticket ML-REG-2329 with reproducer and AST diff.

alice (CS): thanks. next steps for customer: 1) confirm CI passes now that pin is applied; 2) if they want, we can schedule a test window to validate a patched v2.3 with a fix. jose, can you run your CI against the pinned model and report back in this thread?

jose (ACME): running now — CI started, looks like initial compile failures gone. i'll run the full suite, will update in ~20m. thanks for the fast turnaround.

brian (ML eng): internal note: recommend we add a regression test suite for common codegen patterns (TS/Go/python) to the model rollout checklist and add AST equality/coverage checks. putting that on ML-ROLL checklist.

alice (CS): documented action items: CS->confirm with customer, SRE->pin applied (done), ML->investigate & patch, Product->consider rollout gating for code models. owners: alice, tanya, brian.

jose (ACME): CI green. thanks everyone — will flag if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:

alice (CS): closing loop for now. created support ticket IN-ACME-4721 -> escalated -> ML-REG-2329. we'll reopen if issues reappear.
